title: SDK Bridge: Language coverage roadmap & streaming ergonomics intake
creator: Miguel Torres
description: Consolidate inbound customer asks for additional language SDKs and streaming ergonomics into a prioritized, pragmatic roadmap that balances engineering cost, enterprise requirements (SAML/SSO, token rotation, signed releases), and developer ergonomics. Deliver a concrete set of low-risk prototypes (Node + Python streaming improvements) and a cross-language "SDK Bridge" spec to reduce duplication and accelerate later language bindings.
customer_requests: Official Go and Rust SDKs with stable async/await ergonomics
JVM-targeted client (Java/Kotlin) that supports streaming and backpressure semantics
Node SDK: resumable streams, token rotation hooks, smaller browser bundles (ESM), first-class AbortController integration
Python: typed responses (dataclasses/pydantic), synchronous and async parity, streaming SSE/WebSocket ergonomics
Enterprise needs: signed binary releases, long-term support windows, offline install bundles, KMS integration for key rotation
Auth patterns: first-class OAuth device/code flow examples, API key rotation guidance, SSO/SAML integration patterns for tenant onboarding
Streaming features: at-least-once vs exactly-once guidance, client-side caching of KV prefixes, in-band error surface for partial outputs
prioritization_rationale: We weigh customer ARR signal, onboarding friction, engineering cost, and cross-language reuse. Immediate focus on Node and Python streaming fixes because they affect the most customers and unblock enterprise proof-of-concepts. Go and Rust are high strategic value but can be bootstrapped by a common spec + generator to reduce implementation cost. Security-sensitive features (signed releases, KMS hooks) are gate criteria for enterprise GA.
scoring_rubric: Customer ARR impact (0-5): counts committed deals citing SDKs or streaming issues
Onboarding friction (0-5): how many new customers blocked or delayed
Engineering cost (0-5, inverse): time to build and maintain across languages
Reusability (0-5): potential to implement as shared 'bridge' or generator
Security/compliance lift (0-3): additional review or infra required
proposed_solution: Create an "SDK Bridge" specification: a minimal canonical API surface and streaming primitive set (open protocol based on SSE/WebSocket + chunked JSON envelope) plus an auth adapter contract. Implement two reference implementations (Node, Python) that demonstrate: resumable streams, token rotation hooks, AbortController/async iterator semantics, and enterprise packaging (signed artifacts, offline bundles). Parallel small design doc for Go/Rust generator approach; aim to generate idiomatic stubs from the bridge spec to accelerate 2nd-wave languages.
rollout_plan: 2025-02-20 to 2025-03-03: research spike and API design sessions (PM, Eng, DevRel)
2025-03-04 to 2025-03-18: Node + Python prototype implementing streams + token rotation
2025-03-19 to 2025-03-26: internal dogfood with two enterprise customers and Solutions Eng
2025-03-27 to 2025-04-01: finalize spec, security review, docs and SDK beta release
Post-GA: iterate via generator for Go/Rust and staged onboarding for JVM

notes: Trade-offs: fully idiomatic language SDKs vs generated stubs — generator reduces duplication but may need hand-tuning for ergonomics
Risk: signed-release and offline bundle infra could add 2-3 sprints of infra work if not scoped carefully
Mitigation: ship minimal signed artifact flow for beta (GPG signed tarball) and iterate on HSM/KMS integration later
Observation: many customers ask for 'token rotate' hooks; prefer a simple callback pattern on the client rather than embedding rotation logic in SDK
